children.name: Balaeniceps
children.description: A monotypic genus of enormous, stork-like bird with a uniquely massive, shoe-shaped bill that is both its most distinctive feature and its primary hunting tool. The Shoebill is a living fossil, the sole survivor of an ancient lineage of birds. Its slow, deliberate movements and statue-like stillness during hunting have earned it a legendary reputation among African wetland dwellers.

children.name: Balaeniceps rex
children.description: The shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird. It is named for its enormous, shoe-shaped bill. It has a somewhat stork-like overall form and was previously classified as a stork in the order Ciconiiformes, but genetic evidence places it with pelicans and herons in the Pelecaniformes. Adults are mainly grey, while juveniles are browner. It lives in tropical East Africa in large swamps from South Sudan to Zambia.
